solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: In action, press cited for contempt

indicators.note: letters put into action are set moving and rearranged, so these words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Journalists caught out in court are found guilty of contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In action' signals the anagram of PRESS CITED; 'for' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing contempt for someone means treating them with a total lack of regard, a synonym.

clue.text: It gets me upset in the newspaper

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word over so it reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by something they read in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the second word over; the definition is loose, meaning 'a piece found in the newspaper'.
explanation.definitionFit: A single article or report printed in a paper is called an item.

clue.text: Rushes round to see primate

indicators.note: turning the letters round rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone hurries off to visit a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges RUSHES; 'to see' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey, a member of the primate order.

clue.text: Take exam on flourishing poet

parts.note: to sit an exam is to take it
doing well means flourishing

explanation.surface: A thriving poet sitting an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was an English poet; in a down clue 'on' means placed below, so the second piece follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith, Osbert and Sacheverell Sitwell were writers, Edith chiefly known for her poetry.

clue.text: Time to introduce final character in book

indicators.note: the first piece takes in the second, which goes inside it

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The moment has come to bring a story's last character into a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is one of the books of the Old Testament, named after the priest-scribe.

clue.text: Papers — the first editions

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: issues of a magazine are its editions

explanation.surface: Newspapers being the earliest printings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes T from 'the', then ISSUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissues are thin sheets of soft paper, so papers is a plural synonym.

clue.text: Light and delicate piano had us quite excited

indicators.note: excited letters are agitated and jumbled

explanation.surface: A gentle piano piece thrilled the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quite excited' rearranges PIANO HAD US.
explanation.definitionFit: Diaphanous fabric is so fine and light that it is almost see-through.

clue.text: It causes rough weather and loss of trade

explanation.surface: A storm system and a slump in business.
explanation.definitionFit: A depression is an area of low pressure bringing storms, and a long economic slump.

clue.text: Deputy in the grip of depravity

explanation.surface: A second-in-command is caught up in a scandal of moral corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: vice- as in vice-president, the workshop tool that grips, and wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice serves as a prefix for a deputy, names a gripping bench tool, and means immoral conduct.

clue.text: Shares exist in false teeth

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other, as the clue says it is in the teeth

parts.note: dentures are a set of false teeth
to be is to exist

explanation.surface: A strange claim that stock certificates are tucked into someone's dentures.
explanation.definitionFit: Debentures are bonds or loan stock, financial holdings loosely called shares.

clue.text: Are all his shots singles through cover?

definitions.text: Are all his shots singles through cover?

parts.words: Are all his shots singles through cover?
parts.note: reads like a cricket question about a batsman scoring singles through the cover fielding position, but describes a hidden marksman firing single shots from concealment

explanation.surface: A cricket query about a batsman who only ever scores singles through the covers.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position, and singles are one-run shots; the real picture is a concealed rifleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A concealed marksman picks off targets one shot at a time from a hiding place.

clue.text: Letter that is spelt badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A complaint that a written message has poor spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IE (that is) with SPELT.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as with the New Testament letters of Paul.

clue.text: Creatures that ruin the marrows?

indicators.note: ruining something wrecks it, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Pests in the garden that spoil the vegetable crop.
explanation.walkthrough: A marrow is a large British garden squash; 'ruin' rearranges THE MARROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms are soil-dwelling animals, so creatures is a broad category for them.

clue.text: One is certain to be this

definitions.text: One is certain to be this

parts.words: One is certain to be this
parts.note: read as a riddle: something guaranteed never to be wrong is sure, or certain

explanation.surface: A remark that one is bound to be a particular thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain' reads first as 'bound to', but it means 'sure of being right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being incapable of error means being certain to be right.

clue.text: Hail trapped between two points of roof projection

indicators.note: the second piece is caught between the two letters of the first

parts.note: E and S are compass points
ave is the Latin greeting hail

explanation.surface: Hailstones caught at two corners of an overhanging roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' looks like weather but is the Latin greeting AVE, between E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: The eaves are the lower edge of a roof that overhang the walls.

clue.text: They have no choice, poor chaps

explanation.surface: Sympathy for unfortunate men left without options.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition alludes to the proverb 'beggars can't be choosers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially those who must ask for alms cannot choose, and paupers are poor men.

clue.text: Increase in shouts of disapproval at the end of the act

parts.note: boos are shouts of disapproval

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Jeering grows louder when a stage show finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the end of' takes the last letter of 'act'.
explanation.definitionFit: To boost is to increase or raise something, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Falls behind, having gained nothing in old capital

indicators.note: the first word takes on something extra, so the second piece goes inside it

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A runner drops back and loses ground in a former seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: Lagos was Nigeria's capital until Abuja replaced it in 1991.
explanation.definitionFit: This Nigerian city was the nation's seat of government before 1991, a former capital.

clue.text: Craft lacking a prow?

indicators.note: a prow is a vessel's front, so the word loses its front letter

explanation.surface: Asks whether a boat with no bow counts as a proper vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the front letter, C, from CRAFT; the result is a crude floating platform with no shaped bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple floating platform of lashed logs is a vessel without a pointed bow.

clue.text: Withdrawal of 101 meeting points

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the word of is written backwards

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The pulling out of a hundred and one rendezvous spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Withdrawal' turns OF into FO, and 101 is CI in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci are points where lines or rays converge, so meeting points is a fair synonym.

clue.text: It's most desirable to enclose a wild animal

indicators.note: the first piece wraps around the second, as a pen encloses an animal

parts.note: the best is the most desirable

explanation.surface: Advice that a dangerous creature is better kept in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is a creature, especially a wild or savage animal.

clue.text: One never knows what it may hold for the present

definitions.text: One never knows what it may hold for the present

parts.words: One never knows what it may hold for the present
parts.note: reads like uncertainty about the future, but describes a party tub holding hidden gifts

explanation.surface: A thought about the unknowable future.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British lucky dip: presents buried in bran for children to pull out unseen. 'present' means a gift, not now.
explanation.definitionFit: This lucky dip hides gifts in bran, so the person dipping cannot know which they will get.

clue.text: Minor, four, appearing in a court case

indicators.note: the first named piece shows up inside the other

parts.note: a trial is a court case
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A child and three others appear before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor' suggests a child; it means unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is minor, of little importance.

clue.text: They have titles within their grasp

definitions.text: They have titles within their grasp

parts.words: They have titles within their grasp
parts.note: describes champions who currently possess their championships, read literally as people gripping something

explanation.surface: Champions who currently possess their championships.
explanation.walkthrough: Title-holders are reigning champions; the literal grasping picture describes anyone who holds something.
explanation.definitionFit: People who keep possession of a title are its current champions, those who hold it.

clue.text: The reason he left crime

indicators.note: left as in departed, so these letters go away from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Explaining why a man walked out on a life of offending.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing HE from THE REASON leaves T + REASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason, betraying one's country, is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: A Saudi, say, takes the French to be cultivated

parts.note: a Saudi is an example of an Arab
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Saudi man hires a Frenchman to become more refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' suggests refinement; here it means farmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is fit for ploughing and growing crops, that is, able to be farmed.

clue.text: A prayer of three short words

definitions.text: A prayer of three short words

parts.words: A prayer of three short words
parts.note: an old word for a prayer which splits into three little words, or, is and on

explanation.surface: A very brief prayer made up of just three little words.
explanation.walkthrough: Orison, an old word for a prayer, splits as OR IS ON, three short words.
explanation.definitionFit: Orison is an archaic or literary word for a prayer.

clue.text: This large bird reared smaller ones

indicators.note: in a down clue, reared means raised upright, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: auks are smaller seabirds

explanation.surface: A big bird raising its little chicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' suggests raising young; it turns AUKS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A skua is a large predatory seabird.

clue.text: Revered figure in holding company

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An admired person who owns a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding company' looks like a business term; IN holds CO.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a person venerated or idolised, a revered figure.

clue.text: Return a faulty purchase, but apologise

explanation.surface: Taking a broken item back to the shop and saying sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both returning goods to a shop and withdrawing a remark in apology.

clue.text: Harbour a spy

explanation.surface: A port gives shelter to a secret agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole is a stone breakwater, or the harbour it encloses; also a long-term secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a breakwater sheltering a harbour, and also an infiltrated double agent.

clue.text: Certainly using every available method

explanation.surface: Agreeing eagerly to try every possible approach.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite assent like of course and literally using every means.
